## What was tried
This is item C7 of the coordinator issue #716 (next release: the features of issue 655 that the current plan does not cover), split out so it can be built and tracked on its own. Issue 655 was split into its 14 sections and one analyst per section classified every design feature against the unification spec and its decision record; this item is one of the features that were found missing. Nothing in this item is built yet. #716 stays the umbrella issue: its closing review holds the build order, the phases and the open owner decisions.

## Relevant files and links
- Parent issue: #716 (this item is a sub-issue of it). Sister issues of the split: watcher #717, TUI dashboard #718. Source design: #655.
- Current plan (local files, not pushed): `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/spec/SPEC.md` (stages S0 to S17, Appendix B after PR 700), `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/DECISIONS.md` (43 recorded decisions), `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/debates/*/VERDICT.md`, `.dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/spec/FOLLOW-UPS.md`.
- Per-section analysis with every row, status and evidence (local files, not pushed): `.dev/implement/reference-our-research-a-3463b8ef/sections/section-01.md` to `section-14.md`.
- Pull request 697 (closed unmerged revert of PR 682, replaced after PR 700 by PR 701) and the follow-up issues 698 and 699 come from the same review work.

## Done when
The item below is built, tested and checked against its own lines, or the owner records in chat that it is dropped. The text is copied unchanged from #716.

### C7. Worker start: Task, worker-start, issue link, Dispatch id, worktree check, unknown-outcome handling (655 section 2, 6; rows S02-F24, S02-F25, S06-F9, S06-F10)
  - What to build: After the guard binding, the coordinator creates the Orca Task from the filled handoff, starts the worker with `worker-start --task`, attaches the issue with `orca reference add`, checks `worker-show`, and stores the Dispatch id in its state file.
  - Also in this item:
    - S02-F25: When `worker-start` returns an unknown outcome, the coordinator asks Orca whether that request took effect (`request-show`) once, retries only with the same request id, and escalates on the second failure.
    - S06-F9: The coordinator records, with `orca reference add`, the link between an issue, its worktree and its worker, and finds it again with `orca reference find` after a restart.
    - S06-F10: Before `worker-start`, the coordinator runs `orca worktree ps` and refuses to start a worker in a worktree where another agent is live.
  - Done when: a fixture start shows a Task, a Dispatch in `ready`, the issue attached to the worktree (`orca reference list`) and the Dispatch id in `issues/<repo-key>__<N>.json`.
    - also: a fault-injected unknown `worker-start` never produces two Dispatches for one issue and the second failure writes an escalation entry.
    - also: After a restart the coordinator finds the issue's worktree and worker through `orca reference find` and no second worktree or worker is created.
  - Related items (read together; the order is in the review at the end): C5
  - Research and debate results from our documents:
    - S02-F24: .dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/techref/ISSUE-TO-WORK-PIPELINE-TECHNICAL-REFERENCE.md:1360 `no Python in src/ calls worker-start or task-create. Status: NOT BUILT`; same file line 1342 (WC-8, WC-13: a command or worker never calls `worker-start`, `dispatch`, `task-create`).
    - S02-F25: .dev/brainstorms/20261120-pr686-unify/spec/SPEC.md:211 `an unknown launch receipt never relaunches` (FR-21); local check: `orca orchestration request-show` and `worker-start --retry-request` exist (help output).
    - S06-F9: SPEC.md:231 (FR-29) already keeps ONE adoption record per issue, an exclusive-create file; a second record in Orca would be a second store. CLAUDE.md (project instructions, fork rule): Orca link flags (`--issue`, `--pr`) are never passed for this repo until the Orca project id is the fork's; whether `reference add` carries such a link is UNVERIFIED (not found in ~/.claude/skills/orca-cli).
  - Watch out:
    - S02-F24: the worker contract bars commands and workers from `worker-start`, `dispatch` and `task-create` (WC-8, WC-13); FR-27 repeats "never `worker-start`" for a script-started coordinator. Only a person-opened or authorized coordinator session may run these.
    - S02-F25: a blind retry could start two workers in one worktree; keep the plan's no-double-start principle (FR-21, FR-29).


## Pick-up note
- Read the review at the end of #716 first: it holds the build order, the three phases and the owner decisions that gate this item. The related-item ids above (C numbers) refer to the sibling sub-issues of #716.
- The plan files named above are local files, not pushed; read them from a checkout that has them, or ask the owner.
title: [FEATURE] Coordinator C7: Worker start: Task, worker-start, issue link, Dispatch id, worktree check, unknown-outcome handling
